packetName: Mark 6 Safe TMI Hub Route Scaffold Implementation
purpose: Documents verification that the eight route scaffolds requested by the Mark 6 brief (/about, /ecosystem, /consulting, /media, /performance, /distribution, /hero, /partners) were already implemented in the Mark 4 pass and already satisfy every Mark 6 Required/Forbidden constraint verbatim -- so this pass made no source-code, test, navigation, footer, sitemap, or robots change. This document records the verification method, the full route decision matrix, and the validation re-run performed to confirm nothing regressed.

implementationSummary.finding: All eight routes named in the Mark 6 brief already existed on this branch, added in the Mark 4 pass (commit 9186ca5) and unchanged since. A line-by-line comparison of each route's rendered content against Mark 6's per-route 'Required'/'Forbidden' lists found full compliance in every case -- no gap, no missing status string, no forbidden module present.
implementationSummary.actionTaken: No source file, test file, navigation, footer, sitemap, or robots configuration was modified. The full validation gate (typecheck, test, test:unit, check:constants, build in both PUBLIC_PREVIEW modes, ci, test:a11y) was re-run in full and confirmed green, satisfying the brief's 'run all existing relevant validation before and after implementation' instruction where before and after are identical because no implementation change was required.
implementationSummary.whyNoNewTestsWereAdded: Mark 6 asks for narrow tests only 'where needed' to prove a specific list of properties. Every property on that list is already proven by existing coverage: tests/hub-routes.test.ts (Mark 4, 19 tests -- forbidden-conversion-pattern scan, posture-language sourcing, HERO's zero-<a>-elements rule, the four incubation verticals' non-clickable rule, and navRoutes() nav-eligibility) plus the ecosystem-wide generic checks that already run against these same eight routes' built output: scripts/check-public-output.mjs (TBD sentinel, unverified mailto, non-live property hrefs, preview noindex, LinkedIn) and tests/a11y.mjs (0 axe-core violations across all 13 routes, these eight included). Adding a duplicate test would not close a real gap and was avoided per the instruction not to add unrelated changes.

sharedContentModelArchitecture.registry: src/lib/hub-routes.ts (Mark 4) -- a small, typed, local route registry (HubRoute interface: path, navLabel, postureLabel) that is the single source of truth for which routes are nav-eligible and what exact posture string each renders. Header.astro renders navRoutes() from this registry rather than a hand-written link list.
sharedContentModelArchitecture.separationOfConcerns: Consistent with the Mark 6 brief's required four-way separation: (1) neutral approved copy -- static prose written directly in each .astro page, reusing already-approved constants like ORG.boilerplate where applicable; (2) planned-only modules -- explicitly labeled 'not yet populated' / 'not yet built' placeholder divs on Consulting/Media/Performance/Distribution/Partners; (3) proof-dependent modules that remain non-rendered -- no Service module, case study, testimonial, or metric is rendered anywhere, gated behind docs/mark-5-tmi-content-model-and-proof-registry.json's proof-registry IDs which all remain 'absent'; (4) conversion modules that remain absent/inert -- no form, mailto, tel, external link, or CTA exists on any of the eight routes; the homepage's one conditional CTA slot is the sole conversion-shaped element in the entire site and renders nothing while VERIFIED_INBOXES is empty.
sharedContentModelArchitecture.noCmsIntroduced: No content-collection directory, database, remote content fetcher, or new dependency was introduced. This matches the Mark 6 instruction to avoid a generic CMS/database abstraction.
sharedContentModelArchitecture.reuse: Every route reuses Layout.astro (metadata/canonical/robots/JSON-LD), Eyebrow.astro, and the existing .section/.wrap/.divisions-grid/.division/.division-status/.stub-note CSS classes from src/styles/global.css -- no new component or CSS class was introduced for any of the eight routes.
